prompt: Find the slope of the line through $(0, 10)$ and $(5, 0)$.
hint: Look at what happens to $y$ as $x$ grows. That tells you the sign of the slope before you calculate.

hints.text: Look at what happens to $y$ as $x$ grows. That tells you the sign of the slope before you calculate.
The rise is $0 - 10 = -10$ and the run is $5 - 0 = 5$. Divide the rise by the run and keep the negative sign.
$-10 \div 5 = -2$, so the slope of the line is $-2$.

explanation: The rise is the change in $y$: $0 - 10 = -10$. It is negative because the $y$-values fall.
The run is the change in $x$, subtracted in the same order: $5 - 0 = 5$.
Slope is rise over run, so the slope is $\frac{-10}{5} = -2$, a line that goes downhill.

alternativeExplanations.title: Downhill stairs
steps: From $(0,10)$ to $(5,0)$ you drop $10$ while walking $5$ across.
Each step across drops you $2$: the slope is $-2$.
